chapter: Billy Hicks, the Apollo and Roy Eldridge
title: First recording with Roy Eldridge: Muskrat Ramble and High Society
summary: Learning to read music, and his first recording, on Vocalion, with Don Redman arrangements.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What were you saying about learning to read and Clyde Hart?

Yeah, well they used to play checkers between sets, and so Roy would make me go in the room next door, and get the music book, and learn how to read music -- because also, you know, we had arrangements that were written by some great arrangers back in those days, like Don Redman -- you know, like my first record I ever made in my life was with Roy Eldridge, and the arrangements were written by Don Redman.
The first tune I ever recorded was "Muskrat Ramble". That was the first tune I ever recorded, and then "High Society" was the second tune we did on that date; I'll always remember that.
What label did you say that was on, Panama?
That was on the Vocalion label.
Okay, we'll talk about that later.
